title: Geo-Fenced Policy Operator and Evidence Streamer for Retention Drift Detection
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Build a policy-as-code operator that enforces geolocation-specific retention and residency controls and a companion evidence streamer that automatically collects, normalizes, and exports drift and remediation events for audit reporting. The operator must be Kubernetes-friendly for Redwood Private deployments and integrate with the control plane for Hosted/Dedicated. It will continuously evaluate declared policies against live resource configuration and metadata, detect deviations from expected residency/retention settings, attempt automated remediations when safe, and produce tamper-evident evidence bundles for downstream reporting and legal audits.
acceptance_criteria: Operator can parse and evaluate a policy manifest (HCL or YAML) that declares residency zones and retention windows per resource type (sessions, logs, user data blobs)
Drift detector identifies mismatches between declared retention/residency and actual storage metadata with <60s median detection for config changes
Remediation engine can apply safe fixes for non-sensitive resources with configurable approval gates and produce a remediation record
Evidence streamer exports signed, versioned event bundles to S3-compatible endpoints and the Console audit pipeline, with schema v1.0
Security review completed and operator passes RBAC and KMS integration tests for private deployments
Docs include a Minimal Reproducible Example (MRE) and a rollout playbook; end-to-end test coverage >= 70% for critical paths
implementation_steps: Design policy manifest schema and mapping to internal resource types; collaborate with PM and legal on required fields
Prototype a lightweight k8s controller that watches ConfigMaps/CRDs for policy and relevant storage objects for metadata
Implement a drift detection pipeline that snapshots metadata and computes diffs, with exponential backoff for noisy resources
Build remediation primitives: annotate, patch, and create change requests against customer-managed storage and Document approval gates
Create evidence streamer that signs events with service KMS, timestamps them, and writes to configured sinks (S3, GCS, Redshift), plus Console ingestion path
Integrate observability: per-policy metrics, tracer spans, and structured logs; add alerting runbooks
Perform security and compliance review; add hardened RBAC rules and KMS key usage patterns
Prepare docs, CLI examples, and a canary rollout plan for Dedicated and Private customers
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Automated remediation may cause customer outages if applied incorrectly. Mitigation: default to dry-run, require opt-in for auto-remediate, and add canary and staged rollouts
Risk: Evidence tampering concerns. Mitigation: sign evidence bundles with KMS and include immutable sequence numbers plus retention policy on evidence sinks
Risk: High-volume churn (frequent metadata changes) could overwhelm pipeline. Mitigation: implement adaptive sampling and rate-limits, and allow per-policy throttles
Risk: Cross-region policy conflicts. Mitigation: policy precedence rules, explicit region scoping, and conflict detection with clear operator logs
notes: Design discussion notes: drive toward single CRD 'GeoPolicy' that maps to multiple resource selectors. Avoid inventing a full policy DSL; start with declarative constraints for residency and retention.
Compliance input: legal requires evidence bundles to include who/what/when/why, and chain-of-custody for remediation actions. Need to record operator identity and KMS signature.
Integration: Console team will consume evidence via /internal/audit/events; coordinate on schema and ingestion cadence.
Prototype PR: github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/657 (prototype controller, dry-run mode)
Related work: ENG-31234 provides config reconciler foundations we can reuse for snapshotting and evidence formatting
